summary.one_liner: kubectl-ai is a Go command-line assistant that turns natural-language requests into Kubernetes operations using LLMs, runnable as a standalone binary or kubectl plugin.
summary.what_it_does: It translates user intent into kubectl and bash operations, using built-in tools for both and allowing custom tool definitions via a tools.yaml config. It supports many LLM providers, including Gemini (default), Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Grok, AWS Bedrock, and local models through ollama and llama.cpp. It runs in an interactive chat mode that keeps context across questions, or in a one-shot mode with a task passed as an argument. It can act as an MCP client to use tools from external MCP servers, and as an MCP server exposing its kubectl tools to clients over stdio or streamable HTTP, with optional OAuth 2.1 bearer-token auth on the HTTP endpoint. Settings can come from flags, a YAML config file, or environment variables, and a Docker image and web UI option are provided.
use_cases: Ask an AI to run kubectl commands in plain English
Fetch pod logs for an app in a namespace
Use local LLMs like ollama with a Kubernetes cluster
Expose Kubernetes tools to other AI clients via MCP
Aggregate Kubernetes and external MCP tools behind one endpoint
Run a Kubernetes assistant in a Docker container against GKE
how_to_run: curl -sSL | bash  (quick install, Linux and macOS)
kubectl krew install ai  (install via krew)
kubectl-ai --quiet "fetch logs for nginx app in hello namespace"
notable: Supports many LLM providers including local models via ollama and llama.cpp
Works as both an MCP client and an MCP server, aggregating tools from other MCP servers
Optional OAuth 2.1 bearer-token authentication for the HTTP MCP endpoint
Runs as a kubectl plugin (kubectl ai) and as a standalone binary
caveats: The README says it is not an officially supported Google product and is not eligible for the Google VRP
The streamable-http MCP endpoint is unauthenticated unless OAuth flags are set
Some models need the --enable-tool-use-shim flag for tool calling
MCP client mode requires version v0.0.12 or later
